2609.21655.title: Analysing the Linearity of Linguistic Relations in Language Model Embedding Spaces
2609.21655.paper_summary: We propose a framework to analyse how strongly different linguistic relations are linearly encoded in language model embedding spaces. We formalise linear encoding via a constrained linear approximation over related and unrelated word pairs and apply this to an extended BATS dataset covering inflectional, derivational, lexicographic, and encyclopedic relations in GloVe, RoBERTa, and ModernBERT. Our experiments show near-perfect linear encodings for inflectional and derivational relations, but substantially higher errors for lexicographic and encyclopedic relations, especially for one-to-many and many-to-many associations. We also find that RoBERTa and ModernBERT generally encode relations more linearly than GloVe. These results indicate that our framework can reveal which relational structures are most linearly accessible in embeddings, offering a compact tool for probing and comparing relational geometry across models.
2609.21655.paper_summary_zh: 我們提出了一個框架來分析不同語言關係在語言模型嵌入空間中是如何被線性編碼的。我們通過對相關和不相關的詞對進行約束線性近似來形式化線性編碼，並將其應用於擴展的 BATS 數據集，該數據集涵蓋了 GloVe、RoBERTa 和 ModernBERT 中的屈折、派生、詞典和百科關係。我們的實驗顯示屈折和派生關係的線性編碼幾乎完美，但詞典和百科關係的錯誤則顯著較高，尤其是在一對多和多對多的關聯中。我們還發現 RoBERTa 和 ModernBERT 通常比 GloVe 更線性地編碼關係。這些結果表明，我們的框架可以揭示哪些關係結構在嵌入中最具線性可達性，提供了一個緊湊的工具來探測和比較模型之間的關係幾何。
